title: The job interview
settingKo: 면접관이 지원 동기와 경험을 묻습니다.

lines.text: Thanks for coming in. Could you tell me why you're interested in this position?
lines.ko: 와 주셔서 감사합니다. 이 자리에 왜 관심을 갖게 되셨나요?

lines.text: I've spent five years in customer support, and I'm ready to take on a leadership role.
lines.ko: 고객 지원 분야에서 5년을 일했고, 이제 리더 역할을 맡을 준비가 됐습니다.

lines.text: Can you give me an example of a difficult situation you handled?
lines.ko: 어려운 상황을 해결한 사례를 말씀해 주시겠어요?

lines.text: Last year our response times slipped, so I reorganized the schedule and cut waiting times in half.
lines.ko: 작년에 응답 시간이 늘어서 근무표를 재편했고 대기 시간을 절반으로 줄였습니다.

lines.text: That's impressive. How did your team react to the changes?
lines.ko: 인상적이네요. 팀원들은 변화에 어떻게 반응했나요?

lines.text: There was some pushback at first, but they came around once they saw the results.
lines.ko: 처음엔 반발이 좀 있었지만 결과를 보고 받아들였습니다.

phrases.en: I'm ready to take on a leadership role.
They came around once they saw the results.

response.situationKo: 면접관이 가장 큰 약점을 묻습니다. 개선하려는 노력과 함께 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: What would you say is your biggest weakness?

answers.text: I tend to take on too much myself, so I've been learning to delegate more.
answers.noteKo: 약점과 개선 노력을 함께 보여 주는 표준 구조예요.

answers.text: Public speaking used to make me nervous, but I've been working on it by leading team meetings.
answers.noteKo: used to로 과거의 약점이라는 느낌을 줘요.

answers.text: Honestly, I can be a bit of a perfectionist, which sometimes slows me down.
answers.noteKo: 흔한 답변이라 구체적인 사례를 덧붙이면 좋아요.

answers.text: I struggle with saying no, so now I check my priorities before I agree to anything.

title: Talking to the landlord
settingKo: 계속되는 누수 문제를 집주인에게 전화로 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'm calling about the leak in my kitchen. It's been three weeks since I first reported it.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 부엌 누수 때문에 전화드렸어요. 처음 알린 지 3주가 됐어요.

lines.text: I know, and I apologize. The plumber I hired had to cancel twice.
lines.ko: 알아요, 죄송합니다. 제가 부른 배관공이 두 번이나 취소했어요.

lines.text: I understand, but the ceiling is starting to stain and I'm worried about mold.
lines.ko: 이해는 하지만 천장에 얼룩이 생기기 시작해서 곰팡이가 걱정돼요.

lines.text: You're right to be concerned. I'll find someone else who can come by this Friday.
lines.ko: 걱정하실 만해요. 이번 금요일에 올 수 있는 다른 사람을 찾을게요.

lines.text: Thank you. Could you confirm that by email so we both have it in writing?
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 서로 기록이 남게 이메일로 확인해 주시겠어요?

phrases.en: It's been three weeks since I first reported it.
Could you confirm that by email?

response.situationKo: 집주인이 수리를 다음 달로 미루자고 합니다. 예의를 지키면서 더 빨리 해 달라고 요청하세요.
response.prompt: The repair might have to wait until next month, I'm afraid.

answers.text: I understand it's difficult, but this can't wait a month. Could we find a time this week?
A month is too long, honestly. It's getting worse every day.
I'd really appreciate it if this could be fixed sooner, as it's becoming urgent.
answers.noteKo: I'd appreciate it if는 격식 있는 요청 표현이에요.

answers.text: If it can't be sooner, could I get someone myself and take it off the rent?

title: Pushing the deadline
settingKo: 프로젝트 회의에서 일정이 빠듯하다고 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Where are we with the launch? Are we still on track for the fifteenth?
lines.ko: 출시 진행은 어떤가요? 15일 일정 그대로 가능한가요?

lines.text: To be honest, it's looking tight. Testing has taken longer than we expected.
lines.ko: 솔직히 빠듯해 보여요. 테스트가 예상보다 오래 걸렸어요.

lines.text: How much extra time would you need to do it properly?
lines.ko: 제대로 하려면 시간이 얼마나 더 필요한가요?

lines.text: Another week should do it, or we could launch on time with fewer features.
lines.ko: 일주일이면 될 것 같아요. 아니면 기능을 줄여 제때 출시할 수도 있고요.

lines.text: Let me talk to the client and see which option they'd prefer.
lines.ko: 고객과 얘기해서 어느 쪽을 선호하는지 알아볼게요.

phrases.en: It's looking tight.
Another week should do it.

response.situationKo: 상사가 이번 주까지 보고서를 끝낼 수 있냐고 묻습니다. 어렵다고 말하고 대안을 제시하세요.
response.prompt: Can you have the report finished by Friday?

answers.text: Friday might be tight. Could I send you a draft then and the final version on Monday?
answers.noteKo: 거절 대신 대안을 제시하는 좋은 방식이에요.

answers.text: I'll do my best, but I may need until Monday to get it right.
Honestly, I don't think that's realistic with everything else I've got on.
That's a bit of a stretch. What's the most important part to have by then?

title: Performance review
settingKo: 연말 평가 면담에서 상사와 성과와 목표를 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Overall, you've had a strong year. The client dashboard project was a real highlight.
lines.ko: 전반적으로 좋은 한 해였어요. 고객 대시보드 프로젝트가 특히 돋보였어요.

lines.text: Thank you. I learned a lot, especially about managing tight deadlines.
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 특히 빠듯한 마감 관리에 대해 많이 배웠어요.

lines.text: One area to work on is speaking up more in meetings. Your ideas are good, but we rarely hear them.
lines.ko: 개선할 점은 회의에서 더 의견을 내는 거예요. 아이디어는 좋은데 잘 안 들려요.

lines.text: That's fair. I tend to wait until I'm completely sure, and then the moment passes.
lines.ko: 맞는 말씀이에요. 완전히 확신할 때까지 기다리다가 타이밍을 놓치곤 해요.

phrases.en: One area to work on is speaking up more.
phrases.ko: 개선할 점은 더 의견을 내는 거예요.

phrases.en: I tend to wait until I'm completely sure.

response.situationKo: 상사가 내년 목표를 묻습니다. 구체적으로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What would you like to focus on next year?

answers.text: I'd like to take on more client-facing work and improve my presentation skills.
My goal is to lead a small project from start to finish.
I'd really like to focus on mentoring the new hires, if there's an opportunity.
answers.noteKo: if there's an opportunity로 겸손하게 말해요.

answers.text: Honestly, I want to get better at saying no, so I can focus on the important stuff.

title: Pitching to a client
settingKo: 고객사 담당자에게 새 마케팅 계획을 제안합니다.

lines.text: Based on your data, most of your new customers come from short videos, not search ads.
lines.ko: 데이터를 보면 신규 고객 대부분이 검색 광고가 아니라 짧은 영상에서 와요.

lines.text: Interesting. So you're suggesting we move part of the budget to video?
lines.ko: 흥미롭네요. 그럼 예산 일부를 영상으로 옮기자는 거죠?

lines.text: Exactly. We'd start with twenty percent and measure results after three months.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 20퍼센트로 시작해서 3개월 후에 결과를 측정하려고요.

lines.text: That sounds reasonable, but I'll need to run it by our finance team first.
lines.ko: 합리적으로 들리네요. 다만 먼저 재무팀에 확인을 받아야 해요.

phrases.en: So you're suggesting we move part of the budget?
I'll need to run it by our finance team.

response.situationKo: 고객이 비용이 걱정된다고 합니다. 설득해 보세요.
response.prompt: It's a good idea, but I'm worried about the cost.

answers.text: I understand. That's why we suggest starting small with a three-month pilot.
It's a fair concern, but in the long run it should lower your cost per customer.
We can start small and only scale up if the numbers look good.
Totally get it. Let's set a clear budget limit so there are no surprises.

title: Negotiating a better price
settingKo: 거래처 영업 담당자와 계약 가격을 협상합니다.

lines.text: Our price for next year will go up by eight percent because of rising material costs.
lines.ko: 원자재 비용 상승으로 내년 가격이 8퍼센트 오를 예정입니다.

lines.text: I understand costs are rising, but eight percent is more than our budget allows.
lines.ko: 비용이 오르는 건 이해하지만 8퍼센트는 저희 예산을 넘어요.

lines.text: If we sign a two-year contract, could you keep the increase to four percent?
lines.ko: 2년 계약을 맺으면 인상을 4퍼센트로 맞춰 주실 수 있나요?

lines.text: I'd have to check with my manager, but I think five percent might be possible.
lines.ko: 팀장님께 확인해야겠지만 5퍼센트는 가능할 것 같아요.

phrases.en: That's more than our budget allows.
Could you keep the increase to four percent?

response.situationKo: 거래처가 납기를 늦추겠다고 합니다. 조건을 협상해 보세요.
response.prompt: We can deliver, but it'll be two weeks later than planned.

answers.text: In that case, could you send a partial shipment first?
If it's going to be late, we'd expect a small discount.
Two weeks is too long for us. Can you do one week at least?
Hmm, that puts us in a tough spot. What can you do to help us out?

title: Two teammates disagree
settingKo: 의견이 부딪힌 두 팀원 사이에서 팀장이 중재합니다.

lines.text: I feel like Jay keeps changing the design without telling anyone, and it's frustrating.
lines.ko: 제이가 아무한테도 말 안 하고 디자인을 계속 바꿔서 답답해요.

lines.text: Thanks for being honest. I'll talk to Jay as well, so I can hear both sides.
lines.ko: 솔직하게 말해 줘서 고마워요. 양쪽 얘기를 듣게 제이와도 얘기해 볼게요.

lines.text: Maybe we need a simple rule, like posting every design change in the team channel.
lines.ko: 디자인 변경은 전부 팀 채널에 올리는 것 같은 간단한 규칙이 필요할지도요.

lines.text: That would help a lot. I just want to stop finding out at the last minute.
lines.ko: 그럼 많이 도움이 될 거예요. 마지막 순간에 알게 되는 게 싫을 뿐이에요.

phrases.en: I can hear both sides.
I just want to stop finding out at the last minute.
phrases.ko: 마지막 순간에 알게 되는 게 싫을 뿐이에요.

response.situationKo: 동료가 다른 팀원 때문에 불만이 많습니다. 듣고 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: Honestly, I'm tired of doing most of the work on this project.

answers.text: That sounds really frustrating. Have you told them how you feel?
I hear you. Maybe we could divide the tasks more clearly at the next meeting.
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. Would it help if I raised it with the manager?
Ugh, that's not fair. How about we make a task list with names on it?

title: Back to the office?
settingKo: 회사의 주 4일 출근 방침에 대해 동료들과 의견을 나눕니다.

lines.text: Did you see the email? Starting in March, we have to be in the office four days a week.
lines.ko: 메일 봤어요? 3월부터 일주일에 4일 출근해야 한대요.

lines.text: I get why they want more collaboration, but my commute is over an hour each way.
lines.ko: 협업을 늘리고 싶은 건 이해하지만 제 출퇴근이 편도로 한 시간이 넘어요.

lines.text: Same here. I'm actually more productive at home because there are fewer interruptions.
lines.ko: 저도요. 방해가 적어서 오히려 집에서 더 생산적이에요.

lines.text: Maybe we should suggest three days and share some data on our output.
lines.ko: 3일로 하자고 제안하고 우리 성과 데이터를 공유해 보는 건 어때요?

phrases.en: I get why they want more collaboration.
There are fewer interruptions at home.

response.situationKo: 재택근무와 사무실 출근 중 어느 쪽이 좋은지 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's your take on working from home versus the office?

answers.text: Personally, I prefer a mix. Office days for meetings, home days for focused work.
I think it depends on the job. Some roles really need people in person.
Working from home saves time, but on the other hand, I sometimes feel isolated.
answers.noteKo: on the other hand로 반대 측면을 말해요.

answers.text: Home, all the way. No commute, no noise, more sleep!

title: Should I quit?
settingKo: 회사를 그만둘지 고민하는 친구와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: I've been thinking about quitting. I'm not learning anything anymore, and the hours are crazy.
lines.ko: 퇴사를 생각 중이야. 더 배우는 것도 없고 근무 시간도 말이 안 돼.

lines.text: Do you have something else lined up, or would you take a break first?
lines.ko: 다른 자리를 구해 놨어, 아니면 먼저 좀 쉴 거야?

lines.text: Nothing yet. I have enough savings for about six months, though.
lines.ko: 아직 없어. 그래도 6개월 정도 버틸 저축은 있어.

lines.text: It might be smarter to start applying now, so you're not under pressure later.
lines.ko: 지금부터 지원을 시작하는 게 나을지도 몰라. 나중에 쫓기지 않게.

phrases.en: Do you have something else lined up?
So you're not under pressure later.

response.situationKo: 친구가 이직 제안을 받았는데 고민합니다. 조언해 보세요.
response.prompt: They offered me more money, but I'd have to move cities. What would you do?

answers.text: If I were you, I'd think about whether the job itself excites you, not just the money.
answers.noteKo: If I were you, I'd는 조언의 기본 틀이에요.

answers.text: It depends on what matters most to you right now. Is it career or being near family?
Make a list of pros and cons. Sometimes it makes the answer obvious.
Honestly? I'd go for it. You can always move back.

title: Starting over
settingKo: 회계사에서 개발자로 진로를 바꾼 사람과 이야기합니다.

lines.text: So you were an accountant for eight years? What made you switch to coding?
lines.ko: 8년 동안 회계사였다고요? 왜 개발로 바꿨어요?

lines.text: I started automating my spreadsheets, and I realized I enjoyed that more than the actual job.
lines.ko: 스프레드시트를 자동화하다가 본업보다 그게 더 재밌다는 걸 깨달았어요.

lines.text: Wasn't it scary to start from the bottom again?
lines.ko: 다시 바닥부터 시작하는 게 무섭지 않았어요?

lines.text: Definitely, but my finance background turned out to be a huge advantage.
lines.ko: 물론이죠. 그런데 재무 경력이 엄청난 장점이 되더라고요.

phrases.en: What made you switch?
It turned out to be a huge advantage.

response.situationKo: 누군가 지금 일을 왜 선택했는지 묻습니다. 계기를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: How did you end up in your current job?

answers.text: Kind of by accident. I took a part-time job in college, and they offered me a full-time role.
I always loved design, so after graduation I applied to agencies.
I realized I wanted a job where I could help people directly.
Long story! I studied biology but ended up in marketing.

title: Small talk at an event
settingKo: 업계 행사에서 처음 만난 사람과 대화를 이어 갑니다.

lines.text: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Laura, I work in product at a fintech startup.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 처음 뵙는 것 같네요. 로라예요, 핀테크 스타트업에서 프로덕트 일을 해요.

lines.text: Nice to meet you, Laura. I'm Min, a data analyst. What did you think of the keynote?
lines.ko: 반가워요, 로라. 저는 데이터 분석가 민이에요. 기조연설 어떠셨어요?

lines.text: I liked the part about AI in customer service, but it felt a bit like a sales pitch.
lines.ko: 고객 서비스 AI 부분은 좋았는데 좀 영업 발표 같았어요.

lines.text: Ha, I thought the same. Let's connect on LinkedIn and keep the conversation going.
lines.ko: 하, 저도 같은 생각이었어요. 링크드인으로 연결해서 대화 이어 가요.

gist.questionKo: 두 사람이 기조연설에 대해 느낀 점은?

phrases.en: I don't think we've met.
Let's keep the conversation going.

response.situationKo: 행사에서 대화를 마무리하고 연락처를 주고받아 보세요.
response.prompt: It was great chatting. I should probably go say hi to my boss.

answers.text: Great to meet you too. Here's my card. Let's keep in touch.
Of course! Let's connect on LinkedIn. I'll send you a request.
answers.noteKo: send you a request는 친구 신청이에요.

answers.text: No worries! Mind if I email you about that project you mentioned?
Thanks for the chat. I'd love to grab coffee sometime and hear more.

title: A reference call
settingKo: 예전 부하 직원에 대한 평판 조회 전화를 받습니다.

lines.text: Thanks for taking the time. How would you describe Ellie's strengths?
lines.ko: 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다. 엘리의 강점을 어떻게 설명하시겠어요?

lines.text: She's incredibly organized, and clients trust her because she always follows through.
lines.ko: 아주 꼼꼼하고, 항상 끝까지 해내서 고객들이 신뢰해요.

lines.text: Is there any area where she could improve?
lines.ko: 개선할 부분이 있다면요?

lines.text: She sometimes takes on too much herself instead of delegating, but she's aware of it.
lines.ko: 가끔 위임하지 않고 혼자 너무 많이 떠안는데, 본인도 알고 있어요.

phrases.en: She always follows through.
She's aware of it.

response.situationKo: 면접관이 당신의 약점을 묻습니다. 솔직하지만 긍정적으로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: What would you say is your biggest weakness?

answers.text: I tend to be a perfectionist, so I'm learning to set clear time limits.
I used to avoid public speaking, but I joined a club and it's getting better.
Sometimes I say yes to too many things. I'm working on prioritizing better.
Honestly, delegating. I like doing things myself, but I've learned to trust my team.
answers.noteKo: trust my team은 팀을 믿는 거예요.

title: Talking about test results
settingKo: 건강 검진 결과를 의사에게 듣습니다.

lines.text: Your results are mostly fine, but your cholesterol is a little higher than last year.
lines.ko: 결과는 대부분 괜찮은데 콜레스테롤이 작년보다 조금 높아요.

lines.text: Is it something I should be worried about, or can I fix it with my diet?
lines.ko: 걱정해야 할 정도인가요, 아니면 식단으로 고칠 수 있나요?

lines.text: At this level, diet and exercise are usually enough. Let's check again in six months.
lines.ko: 이 정도면 보통 식단과 운동으로 충분해요. 6개월 뒤에 다시 확인해요.

lines.text: Got it. Are there any foods I should cut back on?
lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 줄여야 할 음식이 있을까요?

phrases.en: Is it something I should be worried about?
Are there any foods I should cut back on?

response.situationKo: 의사가 약을 처방하려고 합니다. 궁금한 점을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: I'd like to start you on a low dose of medication.

answers.text: How long would I need to take it?
Are there any common side effects I should watch out for?
Is there an alternative, like changing my lifestyle first?
Do I have to take it forever, or just for now?

title: Making an insurance claim
settingKo: 여행 중 도난당한 노트북에 대해 보험사에 청구합니다.

lines.text: Hi, my laptop was stolen from my hotel room in Rome, and I'd like to make a claim.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 로마 호텔 방에서 노트북을 도난당해서 보험 청구를 하고 싶어요.

lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Did you file a report with the local police?
lines.ko: 안타깝네요. 현지 경찰에 신고하셨나요?

lines.text: Yes, I have the police report and the original receipt for the laptop.
lines.ko: 네, 경찰 신고서와 노트북 원본 영수증이 있어요.

lines.text: Great. Upload both through the app, and we'll usually process it within ten business days.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 둘 다 앱으로 올려 주시면 보통 영업일 10일 안에 처리돼요.

phrases.en: I'd like to make a claim.
Did you file a report with the police?

response.situationKo: 보험사가 청구 처리가 늦어진다고 합니다. 진행 상황을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Your claim is still under review.

answers.text: It's been three weeks already. Could you tell me what's causing the delay?
answers.noteKo: what's causing the delay는 지연 이유를 물어요.

answers.text: When can I expect a decision?
Is there anything else you need from me to speed things up?
Still? Can you at least give me a rough timeline?

title: The rent is going up
settingKo: 집주인이 월세를 올리겠다고 해서 협상합니다.

lines.text: I wanted to let you know that I'm raising the rent by a hundred and fifty from next month.
lines.ko: 다음 달부터 월세를 150 올린다고 알려 드리려고요.

lines.text: That's quite a big jump. I've always paid on time and taken good care of the place.
lines.ko: 꽤 큰 인상이네요. 저는 항상 제때 내고 집도 잘 관리해 왔어요.

lines.text: Would you consider fifty if I sign another two-year lease?
lines.ko: 2년 더 계약하면 50으로 해 주실 수 있을까요?

lines.text: You've been a great tenant. Let's meet in the middle at a hundred.
lines.ko: 정말 좋은 세입자셨죠. 중간인 100으로 하죠.

phrases.en: That's quite a big jump.
Let's meet in the middle.

response.situationKo: 집주인이 계약 갱신을 묻습니다. 조건을 붙여 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Are you planning to renew your lease next year?

answers.text: I'd like to, as long as the rent stays the same.
Yes, if you could fix the bathroom window before then.
I'd be happy to renew. Would you consider a small discount for a longer lease?
Probably! I really like it here. Can we chat about the terms first?

title: My flight was canceled
settingKo: 결항된 항공편의 환불을 상담원에게 요구합니다.

lines.text: We can offer you a travel credit for the full amount, valid for one year.
lines.ko: 전액을 1년간 쓸 수 있는 여행 크레딧으로 드릴 수 있어요.

lines.text: I'd prefer a refund. The airline canceled the flight, not me.
lines.ko: 환불을 원해요. 결항은 항공사가 했지 제가 한 게 아니잖아요.

lines.text: I understand. Let me check your fare type to see if a cash refund is possible.
lines.ko: 이해합니다. 현금 환불이 가능한지 요금 유형을 확인해 볼게요.

lines.text: Yes, you're eligible. It'll go back to your card in five to seven days.
lines.ko: 네, 해당되세요. 5~7일 안에 카드로 들어갈 거예요.

phrases.en: I'd prefer a refund.
You're eligible.

response.situationKo: 상담원이 규정상 환불이 안 된다고 합니다. 단호하지만 예의 있게 요구해 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm sorry, but our policy doesn't allow refunds for this ticket.

answers.text: I understand the policy. However, the cancellation was your decision, so I'd like a refund.
Could I speak to a supervisor, please?
According to consumer law, I'm entitled to a refund when the airline cancels.
That doesn't seem fair. Is there really nothing you can do?

title: That's a lot for a repair
settingKo: 정비소에서 생각보다 비싼 수리 견적을 받습니다.

lines.text: The brakes need replacing, and there's an oil leak. All together, it's about nine hundred.
lines.ko: 브레이크를 교체해야 하고 오일이 새요. 다 합치면 900 정도예요.

lines.text: Wow, that's more than I expected. Which of these is actually urgent?
lines.ko: 와, 생각보다 많네요. 이 중에 정말 급한 게 뭐예요?

lines.text: The brakes, definitely. The leak is small, so it can wait a month or two.
lines.ko: 브레이크는 확실히요. 누유는 작아서 한두 달 기다려도 돼요.

lines.text: OK, let's just do the brakes today, and I'll book the leak for next month.
lines.ko: 좋아요, 오늘은 브레이크만 하고 누유는 다음 달로 예약할게요.

phrases.en: Which of these is actually urgent?
phrases.ko: 이 중에 정말 급한 게 뭐예요?

phrases.en: It can wait a month or two.

response.situationKo: 정비사가 큰 수리비를 말합니다. 견적을 더 자세히 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: It's going to be around twelve hundred to fix everything.

answers.text: Could you break that down for me? I'd like to see the parts and labor separately.
Can I get an itemized quote in writing?
That's a lot. I think I'll get a second opinion first.
Ouch. Which parts can wait, and which can't?

title: Buying a used car
settingKo: 중고차 딜러에게 차에 대해 꼼꼼히 묻습니다.

lines.text: It looks good, but has it ever been in an accident?
lines.ko: 괜찮아 보이는데 사고 난 적 있나요?

lines.text: Just a minor one three years ago. The full history report is right here.
lines.ko: 3년 전에 가벼운 사고 한 번이요. 전체 이력 보고서가 여기 있어요.

lines.text: Would you mind if my mechanic checked it before I make a decision?
lines.ko: 결정하기 전에 제 정비사가 점검해 봐도 될까요?

lines.text: Not at all. Bring it back by five and let me know what you think.
lines.ko: 물론이죠. 5시까지 가져오시고 어떤지 알려 주세요.

phrases.en: Has it ever been in an accident?
Would you mind if my mechanic checked it?

response.situationKo: 딜러가 오늘 계약하면 할인해 준다고 서두릅니다. 시간을 달라고 해 보세요.
response.prompt: If you sign today, I can take five hundred off.

answers.text: Thanks, but I need some time to think about it.
I'd like to sleep on it. Will the offer still be there tomorrow?
I never make big decisions on the spot. I'll let you know by Friday.
Tempting, but not today. I'll call you.

title: Trying to save more
settingKo: 친구와 저축하는 방법에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: How do you manage to save so much? We earn about the same.
lines.ko: 어떻게 그렇게 많이 모아? 우리 버는 건 비슷하잖아.

lines.text: I set up an automatic transfer on payday, so I never see that money.
lines.ko: 월급날 자동이체를 걸어 둬서 그 돈은 아예 안 보여.

lines.text: That's smart. I always plan to save whatever is left, but nothing is ever left.
lines.ko: 똑똑하네. 나는 남는 걸 모으려고 하는데 남는 게 없어.

lines.text: Exactly. Pay yourself first, then live on the rest.
lines.ko: 그러니까. 나한테 먼저 주고 나머지로 사는 거지.

phrases.en: How do you manage to save so much?
Pay yourself first.

response.situationKo: 친구가 돈을 아끼는 방법을 묻습니다. 자신만의 방법을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Any tips for spending less?

answers.text: I track everything in an app, so I can see where the money goes.
What works for me is a weekly budget for food and fun.
answers.noteKo: What works for me로 경험을 공유해요.

answers.text: I stopped buying things online late at night. That alone saved me a lot.
I try to wait forty-eight hours before buying anything non-essential.

title: AI at work
settingKo: 동료와 업무에서 AI를 어떻게 쓰는지 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Are you using AI tools for your reports now? Your summaries have been really fast.
lines.ko: 요즘 보고서에 AI 툴 써요? 요약이 엄청 빨라졌던데.

lines.text: For first drafts, yes. But I always check the numbers myself, because it makes mistakes.
lines.ko: 초안에는요. 근데 틀릴 때가 있어서 숫자는 항상 직접 확인해요.

lines.text: Our team is worried it'll replace junior roles eventually.
lines.ko: 우리 팀은 결국 신입 자리를 대체할까 봐 걱정해요.

lines.text: Maybe some tasks, but I think people who use it well will be in demand.
lines.ko: 일부 업무는요. 그래도 잘 쓰는 사람은 더 찾게 될 거라고 생각해요.

gist.questionKo: 두 번째 사람이 직접 확인하는 것은?

phrases.en: It makes mistakes.
They'll be in demand.

response.situationKo: AI가 우리 일에 미칠 영향에 대해 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you think AI will change your job a lot?

answers.text: I think it'll change some parts, like writing emails, but not the decisions.
It already has. I spend less time on routine tasks and more on planning.
In my opinion, it'll make good workers faster rather than replace them.
Probably! Honestly, I'm a bit nervous about it.

title: A week without social media
settingKo: 일주일 동안 SNS를 끊어 본 친구의 이야기를 듣습니다.

lines.text: So how was your week without social media? Did you survive?
lines.ko: SNS 없는 일주일 어땠어? 살아남았어?

lines.text: The first two days were hard. I kept reaching for my phone without thinking.
lines.ko: 처음 이틀은 힘들었어. 생각 없이 계속 휴대폰에 손이 갔어.

lines.text: But by the weekend, I was sleeping better and I actually finished a book.
lines.ko: 그런데 주말쯤엔 잠도 잘 자고 책도 한 권 다 읽었어.

lines.text: Impressive. Are you going back to it now?
lines.ko: 대단하다. 이제 다시 할 거야?

phrases.en: I kept reaching for my phone without thinking.
phrases.ko: 생각 없이 계속 휴대폰에 손이 갔어.

phrases.en: By the weekend, I was sleeping better.

response.situationKo: 친구가 SNS에 시간을 얼마나 쓰는지 묻습니다. 솔직하게 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: How much time do you spend on your phone every day, honestly?

answers.text: Probably about four hours, which is way too much.
Honestly, it's embarrassing. My screen time says six hours.
I try to keep it under two hours, but it's harder on weekends.
Too much! Mostly short videos before bed.

title: Can anyone afford a home?
settingKo: 친구들과 높은 집값에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Housing prices went up again this year. I honestly don't know how anyone our age can buy a place.
lines.ko: 올해 집값이 또 올랐어. 솔직히 우리 나이에 어떻게 집을 사는지 모르겠어.

lines.text: Most people I know either get help from their parents or move further from the city.
lines.ko: 내 주변은 부모님 도움을 받거나 도시에서 더 멀리 이사 가더라.

lines.text: Moving further out sounds fine until you add two hours of commuting every day.
lines.ko: 멀리 가는 것도 매일 출퇴근 두 시간을 더하면 얘기가 달라지지.

lines.text: True. I think the government needs to build a lot more affordable housing.
lines.ko: 맞아. 정부가 저렴한 주택을 훨씬 더 지어야 한다고 생각해.

options: 정부가 저렴한 주택을 더 지어야 한다

phrases.en: I don't know how anyone can buy a place.
That sounds fine until you add the commute.

response.situationKo: 집을 사는 것과 월세로 사는 것 중 어느 쪽이 나은지 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you rather rent or buy, if you could choose?

answers.text: I'd rather rent for now because I want the flexibility to move.
Buying, eventually. Rent feels like throwing money away.
answers.noteKo: throwing money away는 돈을 버리는 느낌이에요.

answers.text: It depends on the city. In some places, renting makes more financial sense.
Buying, because I want a place I can actually decorate.

title: Book club
settingKo: 독서 모임에서 이번 달 책에 대한 의견을 나눕니다.

lines.text: So what did everyone think? I couldn't put it down for the first half.
lines.ko: 다들 어땠어요? 저는 전반부는 손을 뗄 수가 없었어요.

lines.text: Same, but the ending felt rushed, like the author ran out of ideas.
lines.ko: 저도요. 그런데 결말이 급하게 끝나서 작가가 아이디어가 바닥난 것 같았어요.

lines.text: Really? I thought leaving it open was the whole point.
lines.ko: 그래요? 저는 열린 결말이 핵심이라고 생각했는데요.

lines.text: Maybe, but I wanted at least a hint about what happened to the sister.
lines.ko: 그럴 수도요. 그래도 언니가 어떻게 됐는지 힌트 정도는 원했어요.

phrases.en: I couldn't put it down.
That was the whole point.

response.situationKo: 모임에서 최근 읽은 책이나 본 작품에 대한 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What did you think of it overall?

answers.text: Overall I loved it, but the middle part dragged a bit.
I thought the characters were really well written, especially the mother.
Honestly, the ending made me cry. No spoilers, though!
It started slow, but the second half was brilliant.

title: Parent-teacher meeting
settingKo: 아이의 담임 선생님과 상담을 합니다.

lines.text: Leo is doing well in math, but he's been a bit distracted in class lately.
lines.ko: 레오는 수학은 잘하는데 요즘 수업 시간에 좀 산만해요.

lines.text: I've noticed that at home too. He's been staying up late playing games.
lines.ko: 집에서도 그런 걸 느꼈어요. 게임하느라 늦게까지 안 자요.

lines.text: That would explain it. Maybe a set bedtime would help.
lines.ko: 그래서 그렇군요. 정해진 취침 시간이 도움이 될 것 같아요.

lines.text: We'll try that. Could you let me know in a couple of weeks if things improve?
lines.ko: 그렇게 해 볼게요. 2주쯤 뒤에 나아졌는지 알려 주실 수 있나요?

phrases.en: That would explain it.
Let me know if things improve.

response.situationKo: 선생님께 아이가 학교생활을 어떻게 하는지 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Thanks for coming in. Is there anything you'd like to ask?

answers.text: How is she getting along with the other kids?
Does he participate in class, or is he quiet?
Is there anything we can do at home to support her reading?
Honestly, is he behaving himself?

title: Writing a wedding speech
settingKo: 친구 결혼식 축사를 준비하며 다른 친구에게 조언을 구합니다.

lines.text: I'm giving the speech at Dan's wedding, and I'm freaking out a little.
lines.ko: 댄 결혼식 축사를 하는데 좀 떨려 죽겠어.

lines.text: Keep it under five minutes. One funny story, one sweet story, then raise a glass.
lines.ko: 5분 안으로 해. 웃긴 얘기 하나, 감동적인 얘기 하나, 그리고 건배.

lines.text: Should I mention the time he got lost in Tokyo for six hours?
lines.ko: 도쿄에서 여섯 시간 길 잃었던 얘기 해도 될까?

lines.text: Only if his new wife already knows that story. No surprises at weddings.
lines.ko: 신부가 이미 아는 얘기면. 결혼식에서 깜짝 폭로는 안 돼.

phrases.en: I'm freaking out a little.
Raise a glass.

response.situationKo: 친구 결혼식에서 짧게 축하 인사를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: And now, a few words from a close friend!

answers.text: I've known Dan for fifteen years, and I've never seen him this happy. Congratulations!
Please raise your glasses to the happy couple!
Sarah, thank you for making my best friend so happy. We wish you both the best.
answers.noteKo: wish you both the best는 두 분의 행복을 빈다는 말이에요.

answers.text: Dan, you finally found someone who laughs at your jokes. Don't let her go!

title: Sharing bad news
settingKo: 팀장이 프로젝트 취소 소식을 팀에 전합니다.

lines.text: I wanted to tell you all in person. The client has decided to cancel the project.
lines.ko: 직접 말하고 싶었어요. 고객사가 프로젝트를 취소하기로 했어요.

lines.text: Wow. After four months of work? Does this affect our jobs?
lines.ko: 와. 넉 달이나 했는데요? 저희 일자리에 영향이 있나요?

lines.text: No one is losing their job. We'll move to the new retail project next week.
lines.ko: 아무도 일자리를 잃지 않아요. 다음 주부터 새 리테일 프로젝트로 옮겨요.

lines.text: I know it's disappointing, and I'm proud of what we built.
lines.ko: 실망스러운 거 알아요. 그래도 우리가 만든 것이 자랑스러워요.

phrases.en: I wanted to tell you all in person.
I know it's disappointing.

response.situationKo: 팀장으로서 일정이 늦어진다는 소식을 팀에 알려 보세요.
response.prompt: Team, what's the latest on the launch date?

answers.text: Unfortunately, the launch will be delayed by two weeks because of a security issue.
I'm afraid we'll need to push the launch to next month.
Bad news, guys. We're pushing it back, but it gives us time to fix the bugs.
The date has moved. Here's the new plan, and I'll answer any questions.

title: We made a mistake
settingKo: 잘못된 견적서를 보낸 일로 고객사에 사과 전화를 합니다.

lines.text: I'm calling to apologize. The invoice we sent yesterday had the wrong amount.
lines.ko: 사과드리려고 전화했어요. 어제 보낸 청구서 금액이 잘못됐어요.

lines.text: I noticed that. It was almost double what we agreed on.
lines.ko: 저도 봤어요. 합의한 금액의 거의 두 배였어요.

lines.text: That's completely our fault. I've sent the corrected version, and we've added a check so it won't happen again.
lines.ko: 전적으로 저희 잘못이에요. 수정본을 보냈고 다시는 안 생기도록 확인 절차를 추가했어요.

lines.text: Thanks for calling so quickly. I appreciate that.
lines.ko: 빨리 연락 주셔서 감사해요.

gist.questionKo: 회사는 재발 방지를 위해 무엇을 했나요?

phrases.en: That's completely our fault.
It won't happen again.

response.situationKo: 내가 실수로 회의 자료를 늦게 보냈어요. 동료에게 사과하고 대책을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: We didn't get your slides until after the meeting started.

answers.text: I'm really sorry. That was my fault. Next time I'll send them the day before.
I apologize. I should have checked the time. I'll make sure it doesn't happen again.
Ugh, my bad. I'll set a reminder from now on.
Sorry about that. Is there anything I can do to make up for it?

title: A cultural misunderstanding
settingKo: 외국 동료와 문화 차이로 생긴 오해를 풉니다.

lines.text: Can I ask you something? In the meeting, did I offend you when I disagreed with you?
lines.ko: 하나 물어봐도 돼요? 회의에서 제가 반대했을 때 기분 나빴어요?

lines.text: A little, to be honest. Where I'm from, people usually don't disagree so directly in front of others.
lines.ko: 솔직히 조금요. 제 나라에선 보통 사람들 앞에서 그렇게 직접적으로 반대하지 않거든요.

lines.text: I'm sorry. For us, it's normal and not personal at all.
lines.ko: 미안해요. 우리에겐 그게 평범하고 전혀 개인적인 게 아니에요.

lines.text: I get that now. Thanks for asking. It means a lot.
lines.ko: 이제 이해해요. 물어봐 줘서 고마워요. 큰 의미가 있어요.

phrases.en: It's not personal at all.
It means a lot.

response.situationKo: 외국인 친구가 한국 문화에서 헷갈리는 점을 묻습니다. 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why does everyone ask my age when they first meet me?

answers.text: It's because in Korea we speak differently to older and younger people.
It helps people decide how polite to be. It's not meant to be rude.
answers.noteKo: not meant to be rude는 '무례하려는 게 아니에요'예요.

answers.text: Haha, don't worry! It's just so we know whether to use formal language.
In Korea, age affects how we talk to each other, so it's a natural first question.

title: Organizing a company event
settingKo: 회사 송년회 준비를 동료와 의논합니다.

lines.text: We have about sixty people coming, and the budget is three thousand. Where do we start?
lines.ko: 60명 정도 오고 예산은 3천이에요. 어디서부터 할까요?

lines.text: The venue, definitely. Good places get booked up months in advance this time of year.
lines.ko: 무조건 장소요. 이맘때 좋은 곳은 몇 달 전에 예약이 차요.

lines.text: Should we do a sit-down dinner or something more casual with finger food?
lines.ko: 앉아서 먹는 저녁으로 할까요, 핑거푸드로 좀 편하게 할까요?

lines.text: Casual is better. People can move around and talk to other teams.
lines.ko: 편한 게 좋아요. 사람들이 돌아다니며 다른 팀과 이야기할 수 있으니까요.

phrases.en: Where do we start?
Places get booked up months in advance.

response.situationKo: 팀 행사 아이디어를 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: Any ideas for this year's team outing?

answers.text: How about a cooking class? Everyone works together and we eat what we make.
We could rent a room at an escape game place. It's great for teamwork.
I was thinking we could do a volunteer day instead of a party.
What if we just go bowling and get pizza? Simple but fun.

title: I have an idea for an app
settingKo: 친구에게 창업 아이디어를 설명하고 의견을 듣습니다.

lines.text: It's an app that matches people who want to practice languages with nearby cafés that host meetups.
lines.ko: 언어 연습하고 싶은 사람들을 모임을 여는 근처 카페와 연결해 주는 앱이야.

lines.text: Interesting. How would you make money, though? Users hate paying for apps.
lines.ko: 흥미롭다. 근데 돈은 어떻게 벌어? 사용자들은 앱에 돈 내는 걸 싫어하잖아.

lines.text: The cafés would pay a small fee, because the meetups bring them customers on slow nights.
lines.ko: 카페가 작은 수수료를 내는 거지. 한산한 밤에 손님을 데려다주니까.

lines.text: That's clever. Have you talked to any café owners yet?
lines.ko: 똑똑하네. 카페 사장님들이랑 얘기해 봤어?

phrases.en: How would you make money, though?
That's clever.

response.situationKo: 친구가 아이디어를 말해 줍니다. 좋은 점과 걱정되는 점을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, what do you honestly think of my idea?

answers.text: I like it a lot. My only concern is how you'll get the first users.
answers.noteKo: My only concern으로 걱정을 하나로 좁혀요.

answers.text: It's a great idea, but have you thought about the competition?
Love it! What about testing it with a few friends first?
I'm a little worried it's hard to make money at first, but the concept is strong.

title: Splitting the bills fairly
settingKo: 룸메이트와 공과금을 공정하게 나누는 문제를 이야기합니다.

lines.text: The electricity bill is almost double this month. I think it's the heater in your room.
lines.ko: 이번 달 전기 요금이 거의 두 배야. 네 방 히터 때문인 것 같아.

lines.text: You might be right. I work from home now, so it's on all day.
lines.ko: 그럴 수도 있겠다. 요즘 재택이라 하루 종일 켜 두거든.

lines.text: Would it be fair if you paid sixty percent of electricity in the winter?
lines.ko: 겨울엔 네가 전기 요금 60퍼센트 내는 거 어때, 공평할까?

lines.text: That's fair. I'll also try turning it down when I'm out.
lines.ko: 공평하네. 나갈 땐 온도도 낮춰 볼게.

phrases.en: You might be right.
Would it be fair if you paid sixty percent?

response.situationKo: 여럿이 여행 경비를 나누는데 한 명이 덜 썼어요. 공평한 방법을 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should we just split everything evenly?

answers.text: Maybe not. Since Jin didn't drink, it would be fairer to split the bar bill without him.
answers.noteKo: it would be fairer는 '~가 더 공평해요'예요.

answers.text: How about we split the hotel evenly, and everyone pays for their own food?
Let's use an app that tracks who paid what.
Evenly is easiest, but each person could pay for their own activities.

title: Setting fitness goals
settingKo: 개인 트레이너와 첫 상담에서 운동 목표를 정합니다.

lines.text: So what are you hoping to get out of training? Weight loss, strength, something else?
lines.ko: 운동으로 무엇을 얻고 싶으세요? 감량, 근력, 아니면 다른 거요?

lines.text: Mainly I want more energy. I get tired just climbing the stairs to my office.
lines.ko: 주로 체력을 늘리고 싶어요. 사무실 계단만 올라도 지쳐요.

lines.text: Then we'll focus on cardio and basic strength, three times a week to start.
lines.ko: 그럼 유산소와 기본 근력에 집중하고 처음엔 주 3회로 해요.

lines.text: Sounds good, as long as you go easy on me the first week.
lines.ko: 좋아요, 첫 주만 살살 해 주신다면요.

phrases.en: What are you hoping to get out of it?
Go easy on me.

response.situationKo: 트레이너가 운동이 힘들었는지 묻습니다. 솔직하게 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: How did you feel after yesterday's session?

answers.text: Honestly, I'm really sore today, especially my legs.
It was tough, but I felt great afterwards.
I think it was a bit too intense. Could we slow down a little?
I could barely walk down the stairs this morning, haha.

title: Talking about stress
settingKo: 회사 상담 프로그램에서 상담사와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: You mentioned you've been having trouble sleeping. When did that start?
lines.ko: 잠을 잘 못 잔다고 하셨죠. 언제부터 그랬어요?

lines.text: Around the time I got promoted. I keep checking emails late at night.
lines.ko: 승진했을 때쯤이요. 밤늦게까지 계속 메일을 확인해요.

lines.text: That's very common. What would happen if you stopped checking after nine?
lines.ko: 아주 흔한 일이에요. 9시 이후에 확인을 멈추면 어떻게 될까요?

lines.text: Probably nothing, honestly. I just feel like I have to be available.
lines.ko: 솔직히 아무 일도 없을 거예요. 그냥 연락이 돼야 할 것 같은 기분이에요.

gist.questionKo: 잠을 못 자는 원인으로 보이는 것은?

phrases.en: I've been having trouble sleeping.
I feel like I have to be available.
phrases.ko: 연락이 돼야 할 것 같은 기분이에요.

response.situationKo: 친구가 스트레스를 어떻게 푸는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: What do you do when you're really stressed?

answers.text: I usually go for a long walk without my phone. It clears my head.
answers.noteKo: clears my head는 머리를 비워 준다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: I try to write down everything that's bothering me. It helps a lot.
Honestly? I cook something complicated. It keeps my mind busy.
answers.noteKo: keeps my mind busy는 '딴생각을 안 하게 해'예요.

answers.text: I talk to my sister. She always puts things in perspective.
answers.noteKo: puts things in perspective는 상황을 객관적으로 보게 해 준다는 뜻이에요.

title: Is the course worth it?
settingKo: 동료와 비싼 온라인 자격증 과정에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: I'm thinking about doing that project management certificate, but it's two thousand dollars.
lines.ko: 그 프로젝트 관리 자격증을 딸까 생각 중인데 2천 달러야.

lines.text: Have you asked HR? The company covers training costs if it's related to your role.
lines.ko: 인사팀에 물어봤어? 업무와 관련 있으면 회사가 교육비를 내줘.

lines.text: Really? I had no idea. Is there a catch?
lines.ko: 진짜? 전혀 몰랐어. 조건이 있어?

lines.text: You have to stay for at least a year after finishing, or you pay it back.
lines.ko: 끝난 후 최소 1년은 다녀야 해. 아니면 돌려줘야 하고.

phrases.en: Is there a catch?
I had no idea.

response.situationKo: 상사에게 교육 지원을 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: You wanted to talk to me about something?

answers.text: Yes, I'd like to take a data analysis course. Would the company support it?
I found a course that's directly related to my role. It would help me with our reporting.
Quick ask: could I take two afternoons a month for a class?
I'd like to develop my leadership skills. Is there any training budget for that?

title: Moving abroad
settingKo: 해외 지사 근무 제안을 받고 가족과 의논합니다.

lines.text: The company offered me a two-year position in Singapore. I need to answer by Friday.
lines.ko: 회사에서 싱가포르 2년 근무를 제안했어. 금요일까지 답해야 해.

lines.text: That's huge! How do you feel about it? You've always wanted to live abroad.
lines.ko: 대단하다! 기분이 어때? 늘 해외에 살고 싶어 했잖아.

lines.text: Excited, but nervous about leaving Mom alone, especially after her surgery.
lines.ko: 설레는데 엄마를 혼자 두는 게 걱정돼. 특히 수술 후라서.

lines.text: I'm only twenty minutes away. I can check on her every week.
lines.ko: 나는 20분 거리야. 매주 들러 볼 수 있어.

phrases.en: I need to answer by Friday.
I can check on her every week.

response.situationKo: 외국에서 살아 보고 싶은지, 왜 그런지 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you ever want to live in another country?

answers.text: I'd love to, maybe for a few years, just to experience a different culture.
answers.noteKo: for a few years로 기간을 정해요.

answers.text: I don't think so. I'd miss my family and the food too much.
Definitely! Somewhere warm, like Spain. Who wouldn't?
Perhaps one day, if I could find a job that allowed me to work remotely.

title: Living a bit greener
settingKo: 친구와 집에서 실천하는 환경 습관을 이야기합니다.

lines.text: I've started bringing my own containers when I get takeout. It cuts down on so much plastic.
lines.ko: 포장할 때 내 용기를 가져가기 시작했어. 플라스틱이 엄청 줄어.

lines.text: Don't restaurants find that weird?
lines.ko: 식당에서 이상하게 보지 않아?

lines.text: Some did at first, but now my regular place even gives me a small discount.
lines.ko: 처음엔 몇 곳이 그랬는데 이제 단골집은 할인까지 해 줘.

lines.text: Nice. I've been trying to buy secondhand clothes instead of fast fashion.
lines.ko: 좋다. 나는 패스트 패션 대신 중고 옷을 사려고 하고 있어.

phrases.en: It cuts down on so much plastic.
I've been trying to buy secondhand.

response.situationKo: 환경을 위해 하는 작은 습관이 있는지 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you do anything to be more eco-friendly?

answers.text: I always carry a reusable bottle and a tote bag.
I've started taking the bike to work instead of driving.
Not as much as I should, honestly. I do recycle carefully, though.
I try to buy less in general and repair things before replacing them.
answers.noteKo: repair before replacing은 버리기 전에 고치기예요.

title: Can I speak to a manager?
settingKo: 인터넷 고장이 몇 주째 해결되지 않아 상위 담당자를 요청합니다.

lines.text: This is the fourth time I've called about the same problem. My internet drops every evening.
lines.ko: 같은 문제로 네 번째 전화예요. 매일 저녁 인터넷이 끊겨요.

lines.text: I'm sorry. Let's try restarting the router one more time.
lines.ko: 죄송합니다. 공유기를 한 번 더 재시작해 볼게요.

lines.text: I've done that every time. I'd like to speak to someone who can send a technician.
lines.ko: 매번 했어요. 기사를 보낼 수 있는 분과 통화하고 싶어요.

lines.text: Understood. I'll transfer you to our technical team and mark it as urgent.
lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 기술팀으로 연결하고 긴급으로 표시할게요.

phrases.en: This is the fourth time I've called.
I'll mark it as urgent.

response.situationKo: 상담원이 같은 해결책만 반복합니다. 다음 단계를 요구해 보세요.
response.prompt: Have you tried turning it off and on again?

answers.text: Yes, I've already tried that several times. What's the next step?
I have. Could you please escalate this to a supervisor?
I really appreciate your help, but I'd like to speak with someone from the technical team.
Yep, a hundred times! Is there someone else I can talk to?

title: Congrats on the promotion
settingKo: 같이 지원했던 동료가 승진해서 축하하며 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hey, I just heard. Congratulations on the promotion, you really earned it.
lines.ko: 방금 들었어요. 승진 축하해요, 정말 받을 만했어요.

lines.text: Thanks. Honestly, it feels a bit awkward, since we both applied.
lines.ko: 고마워요. 솔직히 우리 둘 다 지원했으니 좀 어색하네요.

lines.text: I was disappointed at first, but you were the better fit for this role.
lines.ko: 처음엔 실망했지만 이 자리엔 당신이 더 잘 맞았어요.

lines.text: That means a lot. And I'd really like your help leading the next project.
lines.ko: 그 말 정말 고마워요. 다음 프로젝트 이끄는 데 꼭 도와줬으면 해요.

phrases.en: You really earned it.
You were the better fit.

response.situationKo: 친구가 좋은 소식을 전합니다. 진심으로 축하해 보세요.
response.prompt: Guess what? I got into the master's program!

answers.text: Congratulations! You deserve it after all that hard work.
answers.noteKo: You deserve it은 '넌 그럴 자격이 있어'예요.

answers.text: That's amazing! We have to celebrate this weekend.
I'm so proud of you. Which school did you choose?
What wonderful news. I'm truly happy for you.
answers.noteKo: truly happy for you는 진심 어린 축하예요.

title: The neighborhood is changing
settingKo: 오래 산 동네의 변화에 대해 이웃과 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Did you notice the old bakery closed? It's going to be another expensive coffee shop.
lines.ko: 오래된 빵집 문 닫은 거 봤어요? 또 비싼 커피숍이 들어온대요.

lines.text: I know. It's nice that the area is safer now, but rents have gone through the roof.
lines.ko: 알아요. 동네가 안전해진 건 좋은데 월세가 천정부지로 올랐어요.

lines.text: A lot of the families who've lived here for decades can't afford it anymore.
lines.ko: 수십 년 산 가족들이 이제 감당을 못 하고 있어요.

lines.text: It's a shame. The neighborhood is losing its character.
lines.ko: 안타까워요. 동네가 자기 색깔을 잃고 있어요.

phrases.en: Rents have gone through the roof.
It's losing its character.

response.situationKo: 살고 있는 동네의 장단점을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's your neighborhood like?

answers.text: It's quiet and green. The downside is that it's far from the subway.
The best part is the food. There are amazing restaurants on every corner.
It's very convenient, but it can get noisy on weekends.
It's a family-friendly area with good schools, although parking is difficult.

title: Accepting an offer
settingKo: 입사 제안을 받고 시작 날짜와 조건을 조율합니다.

lines.text: We'd love to have you join us. Can you start on the first of next month?
lines.ko: 함께해 주시면 좋겠어요. 다음 달 1일에 시작할 수 있나요?

lines.text: I'm excited to accept. I do need to give my current employer four weeks' notice, though.
lines.ko: 기쁘게 수락할게요. 다만 현 직장에 4주 전 통보를 해야 해요.

lines.text: That's fine. Shall we say the fifteenth instead?
lines.ko: 괜찮아요. 그럼 15일로 할까요?

lines.text: Perfect. Could I also confirm that I can work from home on Fridays?
lines.ko: 좋아요. 금요일 재택근무가 가능한 것도 확인할 수 있을까요?

phrases.en: I need to give four weeks' notice.
Shall we say the fifteenth instead?

response.situationKo: 회사가 입사 제안을 했는데 생각할 시간이 필요해요. 정중하게 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, what do you think? Can we expect your answer today?

answers.text: Thank you so much for the offer. Could I have a few days to consider it?
I'm very excited, but I'd like to discuss it with my family. Can I let you know by Monday?
I appreciate it. I just want to think it through carefully before I commit.
answers.noteKo: think it through는 끝까지 생각해 보다예요.

answers.text: Love it so far! Just give me the weekend to sleep on it?
